questions: Does the modulo value need to be read from the input, or is it a fixed constant like 10^9+7?
Are paths considered distinct if they visit the same sequence of blocks but start at different initial blocks?
Is the order of moves considered? That is, are two sequences of moves (e.g., right then up vs. up then right) considered different paths if they start at the same block and end at the same block?
Does 'any number of times (possibly zero)' mean that just standing at the initial block (with no moves) is a valid path?
Are blocks defined only at integer coordinates (x,y) where L ≤ x ≤ R and D ≤ y ≤ U, given the conditions are not fully stated in the prompt?
When moving, must the destination block satisfy the same conditions as the initial block (i.e., within the rectangle defined by L,R,D,U)?
Is the output the total number of possible paths modulo some value, and if so, what is that modulus?
Do the constraints imply that blocks exist at all lattice points in the rectangle [L,R] × [D,U]?
